punchline: Marcus Aurelius wrote that a worse plague than any in the air is a corrupted mind.
thirty_sec: From the mid-160s an epidemic swept the Roman world while Marcus Aurelius ruled. A later biography says the dead were carted away and that funerals for the poor were paid from public funds. In his own notebook, Marcus wrote that the corruption of the mind is a greater plague than any change in the air, and it was the one he could still tend.
key_contrast: Plague of the air, plague of the mind
